documents.title: Using AI Technology Guidelines
documents.summary: Campus-wide Faculty Development Center guidelines giving a rationale and four short principles on support, verification of AI output, academic integrity and data protection. It sets no allow or ban rule and says instructors should give clear guidance.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines never allow or ban AI; they say "Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use" and only ask all users to verify output, be transparent and protect data, so the decision is left to instructors.

units.why: The rationale sets the purpose: GAI "has the power to facilitate and disrupt" teaching, learning and research and needs a "reflective approach"; this is an institution-level framing, so P56 (framework/preamble).
units.anchor: CSUF is committed to supporting teaching, learning, research, and service.

units.why: The sentence names "biases and inaccuracies in AI output" and "ethical use" as concerns that require a reflective approach; it is a statement of ethical concern, so P53 fits.
units.anchor: consideration of biases and inaccuracies in AI output, as well as ethical use of these

units.why: The community "should be transparent about its use" of generative AI, a general disclosure expectation (P24) without specifying format; the modality is "should".
units.anchor: should be transparent about its use

units.why: "Provide ongoing support for the responsible use of Generative AI by faculty, staff, and students" is a commitment to training and support, closest to P63 (support in learning AI) though it also names students.
units.anchor: Provide ongoing support for the responsible use of Generative AI by faculty, staff, and students.

units.why: "all users must review and verify AI generated content" because AI is "prone to inaccuracies, biases, and omissions": verify-output type P31, binding all users, modality must.
units.anchor: all users must review and verify AI generated content before using it

units.why: States that "Generative AI detectors ... have been proven to be unreliable and biased", which is the do-not-rely-on-detectors type P39; it is a factual statement so modality informs.
units.anchor: This includes Generative AI detectors, which have been proven to be unreliable and biased.

units.why: Requires "conforming to CSUF policy" and keeping the "authenticity of academic work or assessments"; the nearest type is P29 (students own what they submit). P36 does not fit since no misconduct classification is stated.
units.anchor: ensuring that AI assistance enhances learning and scholarly and creative activity without compromising the authenticity

units.why: "Maintain transparency in the integration of AI tools" for teaching and service is a disclosure expectation (P24) that reaches instructors as well as students.
units.anchor: Maintain transparency in the integration of AI tools for teaching, scholarly and creative activity, and

units.why: "Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use" asks instructors to state expectations, matching P09 (state AI expectations in syllabus/assignments), modality should.
units.anchor: Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use.

units.why: "Prioritize safeguarding confidential information and user intellectual property" by following data security and privacy policies: protect confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: safeguarding confidential information and user intellectual property by following established policies on data security and

units.why: Asks the community to "recognize and guard against AI-driven phishing attempts or scams"; this is security awareness against AI-enabled attacks, not data protection in AI tools (P50) or any other listed type.
units.anchor: educate users to recognize and guard against AI-driven phishing attempts or scams
units.uncovered_note: Vigilance and education against AI-driven phishing and scams (cybersecurity awareness).

documents.title: Creating a Generative AI Policy
documents.summary: FDC instructor guidance on writing syllabus AI policies, with three sample models (no AI, minor use, by assignment), an assignment-level example, and a five-level AI continuum. It also lists assessment-redesign advice.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Each faculty member is empowered to determine the appropriate use of these tools in their classes" and offers templates and a five-level continuum for them to choose from, so it delegates and lists tiers.

units.why: "Each faculty member is empowered to determine the appropriate use of these tools in their classes and even individual assignments": per-instructor and per-assignment rule, P04.
units.anchor: Each faculty member is empowered to determine the appropriate use of these tools in their

units.why: Calls "transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions" "essential"; instructors must communicate rules in syllabi, so P09, modality should.
units.anchor: Including transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions specifying under what circumstances the use

units.why: "Students must adhere to the syllabus" for AI/Tech use per "policies set by the faculty": student duty to follow the instructor-set rule, which is P04 (instructor sets the rule) rather than P29.
units.anchor: Students must adhere to the syllabus to ensure their usage of AI/Tech tools in their

units.why: Lists "Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden" as a consideration for syllabi: asks instructors to state expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden
units.policy: Instructors consider stating in the syllabus under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden.

units.why: Lists "How students should cite or credit AI" as an item for the syllabus policy; disclosure/citation, P24.
units.anchor: How students should cite or credit AI
units.policy: Instructors consider stating in the syllabus how students should cite or credit AI.

units.why: Suggests a notice about ethical use and a warning about hallucination ("creation of false information"); the content is that AI output can be false, P31.
units.anchor: A notice about using AI ethically and responsibly
units.policy: Instructors consider including in the syllabus a notice about using AI ethically and responsibly, with a warning about hallucination (creation of false information).

units.why: "Discussion of the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content" keeps AI in service of learning; students remain the thinker, P32 (P41 is about practice building skill, not stated here).
units.anchor: Discussion of the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to

units.why: Asks for "a description of how you will authenticate student work ... as required by UPS 300.004"; authentication of student work fits no type exactly (P34 requires interviews or reviews that are not named).
units.anchor: A description of how you will authenticate student work where relevant
units.uncovered_note: Syllabus must describe how the instructor will authenticate student work, as required by campus policy UPS 300.004.

units.why: Encourages faculty to use the boilerplate "as a reflective starting point, thoughtfully considering how AI use may differ across assignments": per-assignment variation set by instructor, P04.
units.anchor: thoughtfully considering how AI use may differ across assignments, learning activities, and disciplinary contexts

units.why: Sample language "students must be the author of all work. The use of generative AI, such as ChatGPT, is not permitted": a ban on AI for all work, P01.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI, such as ChatGPT, is not permitted.

units.why: Sample language says use "will be considered a violation of the CSUF Academic Dishonesty Policies and may be subject to disciplinary action": classes AI use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Use of these tools will be considered a violation

units.why: Notes tools like "Grammarly", "Canva" and "Microsoft Word and PowerPoint" have AI features; this concerns AI built into everyday software, so P07 fits (P18 is about prose rules, not the embedded-tool issue).
units.anchor: As educators, it's essential to be aware that many tools students use daily incorporate AI

units.why: "consider specifying whether the use of such AI tools is allowed or prohibited" asks instructors to be explicit about embedded AI tools per assignment, P07.
units.anchor: When creating assignments, consider specifying whether the use of such AI tools is allowed or

units.why: Example direction allows "AI tools like Grammarly for grammar checks or Canva for design elements"; grammar and writing tool use, P18.
units.anchor: For this assignment, you may use AI tools like Grammarly for grammar checks or Canva

units.why: Example direction: "do not use AI tools like ChatGPT for generating text or Microsoft Copilot for drafting content"; students may not have AI produce submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: Please do not use AI tools like ChatGPT for generating text or Microsoft Copilot for

units.why: The minor-use model says "You may use AI in some minor ways" while students "must be the author of all work": limited default permission, P02 (a ban or tier name would not fit).
units.anchor: You may use AI in some minor ways.

units.why: Template examples of acceptable use include "generate ideas ... create an outline of an essay": brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: generate ideas, polish or edit text you have drafted, create an outline of an essay

units.why: Template examples of acceptable use include "review content, quiz yourself, or for other studying purposes": study aids, P14.
units.anchor: review content, quiz yourself, or for other studying purposes

units.why: Template says students may NOT use AI "for any purpose while taking a quiz or test": P22.
units.anchor: for any purpose while taking a quiz or test

units.why: Template lists as not allowed: "generate content that is directly used in an assignment (such as code, text, images, or other media)" and writing drafts or solving problems; the submitted work is AI-made, P19.
units.anchor: generate content that is directly used in an assignment (such as code, text, images, or

units.why: "Always review individual assignments for specific instructions": rules vary by assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Always review individual assignments for specific instructions.

units.why: Optional template statement: AI language must be attributed "by putting that language in quotation marks and adding a citation": P24 (disclosure/citation).
units.anchor: you must properly attribute that use by putting that language in quotation marks and adding

units.why: The by-assignment model says "students are permitted to integrate AI into some of the substantive work of the course" and to review each assignment; it hands the decision to the assignment, P04.
units.anchor: In this course, students are permitted to integrate AI into some of the substantive work

units.why: "Review individual assignments to determine permissible uses": per-assignment rules, P04.
units.anchor: Review individual assignments to determine permissible uses.

units.why: "you should be able to demonstrate how you contributed to an assignment": students must show their own contribution, P29 (P30 is about explaining every line, which is not stated).
units.anchor: Unless otherwise noted, you should be able to demonstrate how you contributed to an assignment.

units.why: Example faculty requirement: "keep drafts of assignments and generative AI logs that demonstrate how you used AI": logs and drafts, P26.
units.anchor: you are required to keep drafts of assignments and generative AI logs that demonstrate how

units.why: Restates the guidelines that the community "should be transparent about its use" of generative AI; a general disclosure expectation, P24. Coded here because each document is coded on its own.
units.anchor: should be transparent about its use

units.why: The ETHICAL Principles framework is "a flexible and adaptable foundation for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence" and "intentionally avoids rigid definitions": an institution-level framework, P56.
units.anchor: flexible and adaptable foundation for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence

units.why: "The AI continuum ... may also assist you in thinking about crafting your AI policy" offers named levels from No AI to AI Exploration, P05.
units.anchor: The AI continuum presented below may also assist you in thinking about crafting your AI

units.why: "If you allow AI use in your course, remind students about the rules for AI use on every assignment" is a repeated-communication duty for instructors, P09.
units.anchor: If you allow AI use in your course, remind students about the rules for AI

units.why: The "No AI" level: "AI use is not permitted at any stage of this assessment"; a named tier, so P05 rather than P01.
units.anchor: AI use is not permitted at any stage of this assessment.

units.why: No AI level adds that work is done "independently in a controlled environment" relying on "your own knowledge"; tier description, P05.
units.anchor: All work must be completed independently in a controlled environment, relying solely on your own

units.why: "AI for Planning": "AI may be used only during the planning stages, not in the final product"; a named tier that permits narrow uses, P05.
units.anchor: AI may be used only during the planning stages, not in the final product.

units.why: Planning tier allows "brainstorm, organize ideas, or explore directions before writing"; brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: You may use AI tools to brainstorm, organize ideas, or explore directions before writing.

units.why: Planning tier: "all submitted work must be your own original creation": P29 (submitted work is the student's own).
units.anchor: However, all submitted work must be your own original creation.

units.why: "You may be asked to disclose how AI was used and reflect on what you learned": reflection and disclosure, P26.
units.anchor: You may be asked to disclose how AI was used and reflect on what you

units.why: "AI as a Collaborator": "AI may assist with certain tasks, but must be critically evaluated and revised"; a named tier, P05.
units.anchor: AI may assist with certain tasks, but must be critically evaluated and revised.

units.why: Collaborator tier lets students use AI "for drafting, generating ideas, receiving feedback, or refining language"; AI-drafted content is allowed with review, so P16 (generation under conditions) rather than P15.
units.anchor: You can use AI for drafting, generating ideas, receiving feedback, or refining language.

units.why: "all AI-generated content must be reviewed, edited, and adapted by you": verify and take ownership, P31.
units.anchor: However, all AI-generated content must be reviewed, edited, and adapted by you.

units.why: "You may be required to submit evidence of how AI was used, such as prompts, outputs, and revisions": P26 (records submitted).
units.anchor: You may be required to submit evidence of how AI was used, such as prompts,

units.why: "Full AI Integration": "AI can be used throughout the task as a co-creator"; a named tier that permits AI broadly, P05.
units.anchor: AI can be used throughout the task as a co-creator, with thoughtful direction.

units.why: Full integration requires that students "guide their use and demonstrate your own critical thinking": students stay primary problem-solver, P32.
units.anchor: as long as you guide their use and demonstrate your own critical thinking

units.why: "Proper citation and documentation of AI interactions may be required": P24.
units.anchor: Proper citation and documentation of AI interactions may be required.

units.why: "AI Exploration": "AI is used creatively and innovatively to explore new possibilities"; top tier, P05.
units.anchor: AI is used creatively and innovatively to explore new possibilities.

units.why: This tier involves "co-designing assessments where students and educators work together" and customizing GPTs; assessment design with AI, P35.
units.anchor: This level involves co-designing assessments where students and educators work together to explore unique AI

units.why: Advises "Make discussions actual discussions" and retiring "post once, reply twice": redesigning assessments to defend against AI cheating, P35.
units.anchor: Make discussions actual discussions.
units.policy: Instructors make online discussions real interaction (peer review, debating applied examples, collaborative problem solving) instead of the "post once, reply twice" formula.

units.why: Advises "scaffolding projects, integrating process-based feedback and using mastery-based grading" so doing the work is easier than faking it; grading redesign, P35.
units.anchor: scaffolding projects, integrating process-based feedback and using mastery-based grading when possible

units.why: Advises "Teach small, even when the class is big", with small groups and project teams so students are "less likely to ask a chatbot to do their thinking"; course structure redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Teach small, even when the class is big.
units.policy: Instructors teach small even in big classes (flipped lectures, small groups, vertically integrated project teams) so students are less likely to ask a chatbot to do their thinking for them.

documents.title: CSUF's AI Policy
documents.summary: Library guide answering students that CSUF has no campus-wide AI policy and that each instructor decides. It points to general guidelines and an ethical framework.
documents.stance_why: It states "There is no campus-wide policy on AI at CSUF" and "up to your individual Instructor", handing the decision to instructors.

units.why: States "There is no campus-wide policy on AI at CSUF!": a statement of the university default, delegating to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: There is no campus-wide policy on AI at CSUF!

units.why: "Whether AI is allowed or prohibited in your class is up to your individual Instructor": instructor decides, P04.
units.anchor: Whether AI is allowed or prohibited in your class is up to your individual Instructor.

units.why: Gives the reason "there needs to be flexibility according to class goals" with Art and English examples; rationale for instructor discretion, P04.
units.anchor: This makes sense; there needs to be flexibility according to class goals.

units.why: "always follow whatever your Instructor states is the class policy on AI (verbally in class or in writing on the syllabus)": student must follow the course rule, P04.
units.anchor: always follow whatever your Instructor states is the class policy on AI

units.why: "CSUF does provide some general advice and guidelines on AI" points to the guidelines, ethical-use pages and framework; institution-level framework pointer, P56.
units.anchor: CSUF does provide some general advice and guidelines on AI:

No computing-unit or school policy found; course layer deferred. One sentence of the guidelines page is repeated on the creating-policy page and was coded there too since each document is coded on its own.
